Coarse-grain multilevel data to aggregation scale m

Source: R/rg-flow.R
rg_coarse_grain.Rd

Applies the coarse-graining operator T_m: within each cluster, units are randomly partitioned into blocks of size m and each block is replaced by its mean. The cluster structure is preserved, so every scale keeps the same clusters and two scales remain comparable cluster-by-cluster.

Usage

rg_coarse_grain(
  data,
  m,
  treatment = "A",
  mediator = "M",
  outcome = "Y",
  cluster = "cluster"
)

Arguments

data

Data frame with the treatment, mediator, outcome, and cluster columns.

m

Positive integer block size. m = 1 returns the unit scale unchanged.

treatment, mediator, outcome

Character: column names of A, M, Y.

cluster

Character: column name of the cluster identifier.

Value

List with Z (numeric matrix of coarse-grained units, columns A, M, Y) and cluster (their cluster labels).

Details

Blocks are complete by construction: within a cluster of size n_s, the final incomplete block is discarded, so the number of coarse-grained units is sum(floor(n_s / m)), not n / m. Clusters smaller than m drop out entirely at that scale. The composition property T_{m2}(T_{m1}(.)) = T_{m1 * m2}(.) holds exactly on the units a partition retains.

This function calls sample.int() and is therefore random. It never sets a seed; seed the caller (or wrap in withr::with_seed()) for reproducibility.

Examples

set.seed(1)
d <- data.frame(
  A = rnorm(200), M = rnorm(200), Y = rnorm(200),
  sch = rep(1:20, each = 10)
)
cg <- rg_coarse_grain(d, m = 5, cluster = "sch")
nrow(cg$Z)  # 40 = 20 clusters * floor(10 / 5)
#> [1] 40
